title: A triaged review tick re-dispatches instead of closing behind its recorded decision
description:
findings.go tells the operator that after triage 'the close is the only step left'. That is not what happens. closeRoleTick (rolejob.go) marks the tick REJECTED, and on resume processRoleJob -> claimDispatch never reads the recorded role decision, so a zero-commit review is dispatched again.

Measured, on this epic: pxc ran attempts 9, 10 and 11 on BYTE-IDENTICAL SOURCE. Three full frontier reviews of the same diff.

The loop's termination condition is the alarming part. Each re-dispatch pays for a new review, a new review can raise new findings, new findings raise a new hold — so THE LOOP ENDS ONLY WHEN A REVIEWER REPORTS NOTHING. The system is structurally biased toward the review that finds least, and it pays frontier-tier money to get there. A thorough reviewer is punished with another round; an incurious one ends the epic.

It also corrupts the record. recordDecision's role+tick dedup leaves decisions/ holding ATTEMPT 9's answer while a later attempt's close is what ends the tick. So the durable decision belongs to one review and the close belongs to another — and attempt 9's answer is the NOT READY one that b50 says is already spelled 'ready-to-merge'.

No test resumes a triaged role tick, which is why none of this was caught.

Work:
- On resume, a role tick whose decision is recorded and whose findings are triaged CLOSES behind that decision. It is not re-dispatched.
- The recorded decision and the close must belong to the same attempt, or the record says one thing happened and another did.
- Test: triage a review's findings, resume, and assert the review is NOT dispatched again and the tick closes behind the recorded answer.

Related: aqm (which removes most of the occasions this fires), b50 (the verdict it mis-records).

From pxc, third pass — the review found its own loop.
acceptance_criteria: Resuming after triaging a role tick's findings closes it behind its recorded decision without re-dispatching, with the decision and the close belonging to one attempt, covered by a test
